q: A six-storey building lacks an elevated water tank. What provides its water pressure instead?
n: A hydro-pneumatic (pressure) tank substitutes for an elevated tank by using compressed air to pressurize the water supply.

q: Why does gravity-fed water flow stop before reaching a certain point in the distribution system?
o: The volume of water is too little
The booster pump cannot reach the upper level
The water has equalized with the level of its source
The supply is fed from a lower level
n: Gravity-fed flow stops once the water level in the distribution point equals the level of the source — pressure runs out at that point.

q: When water is pumped from a cistern up to an elevated tank and then flows down by gravity, what is this arrangement called?
ref: Water supply systems — feed system types
n: Moving water from a cistern up to an elevated tank, then letting it feed down by gravity, is the indirect downfeed arrangement.

q: What term applies when main-line water is first stored in a cistern, then pumped upward under pressure?
ref: Water supply systems — feed system types
n: Storing water in a cistern first, then pushing it upward by pump, is the indirect upfeed arrangement.

q: Which pump is added to a house supply line to raise weak water pressure from the street main?
n: A booster pump sits on the incoming line and adds pressure when the main is weak. A sump pump empties pits, and a jockey pump keeps a fire line pressurized.

q: Which pump type, using a spinning impeller, is the usual choice for lifting water in high-rise buildings?
n: Centrifugal pumps give steady flow at high capacity. For very tall buildings they are staged or set in multistage units to reach the needed head.

q: A submersible pump is built to be installed where?
n: Submersible pumps are built to operate fully underwater, which is why they're used inside deep wells.

q: Which type of water heater heats water only while a tap is open, with no storage tank?
o: Solar water heater with a tank
Hot-water boiler with a storage cylinder
n: A tankless heater fires its gas burner or electric element only when flow is sensed, so it has no standby loss. Storage and solar types keep a tank of hot water ready.

q: What is usually built directly beneath a pump room?
n: The cistern stores water from the main at ground or basement level. The pump room sits over it so the pumps can draw water with a short suction line.

q: What term names the banging noise heard inside pressurized pipes when flowing water is suddenly stopped?
n: Water hammer is the banging or knocking sound from a sudden pressure surge when flowing water is abruptly stopped or redirected.

q: What fitting is installed specifically to absorb and prevent that banging effect in pipes?
n: A water hammer arrestor absorbs the pressure spike with a cushioned air chamber, preventing the banging effect.

q: What type of valve blocks flow using a flat disk that lowers perpendicular to the pipe's flow path?
n: A gate valve uses a flat disk (gate) that lowers perpendicular to the flow path to fully block it.

q: Which valve opens on its own to release pressure from a boiler or water heater once a safe limit is passed?
n: A relief valve is spring-loaded and opens automatically at its set pressure. A blow-off valve is opened by hand to flush sediment out of the boiler.

q: Which valve lets water flow in one direction only and closes against backflow?
n: A check valve has a swing disc or spring-loaded poppet that the flow pushes open. Reverse flow pushes it shut.

q: Which valve sends water through an S-shaped path, making it good for throttling but causing a large pressure drop?
n: In a globe valve, the water turns and passes up through a seat. This makes it easy to regulate but costs pressure. A gate valve gives a straight, full-bore path when open.
